name: Google Cloud
designation: member of Google Cloud for Web3 Startups
guidance: three.ws is a member of Google Cloud for Web3 Startups. Say that and nothing grander: it is a programme membership, not an endorsement, certification, partner tier or investment. Google Cloud Marketplace is not a listing; never say three.ws is listed, available or live there. What is true and checkable is the engineering: the open 3D model workers run as Cloud Run GPU services (NVIDIA L4), the garment builder is a CPU Cloud Run service whose reference photos come from Vertex AI, and CAD Forge builds on a Cloud Run gen2 service with its own sandbox. Name those pieces plainly and tie each to a fact. Do not say the whole platform runs on Google Cloud, do not say Gemini is an agent brain (that is announced, not shipped), and do not mention credits, grants or amounts. Never claim the Forge generates a model live in the film: the reel shows the engine lanes and tiers, not a finished generation.

features.title: Forge engines on our own Cloud Run GPU workers
features.summary: The Forge turns a text prompt, photos or a sketch into a textured 3D model, and the open models behind it (TRELLIS, Hunyuan3D, TripoSG) run as our own Cloud Run services on NVIDIA L4 GPUs in us-central1. Each tier shows a free lane and a live time estimate before you press Generate, a sketch has its own lane, and the free NVIDIA NIM lane stays behind the self-hosted workers as a safety net. This is the Google Cloud for Web3 Startups programme at work: the GPU workers are the infrastructure it backs.

features.title: The wardrobe: rigged garments built on a Cloud Run pipeline
features.summary: The wardrobe is an open catalog of rigged 3D garments that bind to any humanoid avatar at runtime. New pieces come from garment-forge, a CPU-only Cloud Run service that chains the GPU workers: the reference photo for each piece is made on Google Vertex AI, then the mesh is built, placed on the body, rigged, validated and published. Browse the catalog, open a piece in 3D and turn it around.

features.title: CAD Forge: a real part from one sentence, on Cloud Run
features.summary: CAD Forge writes a build123d program from a sentence and builds it into a real B-rep part on the OpenCascade kernel, then returns STEP, STL, GLB, a drawing sheet and the kernel measurements. The builder is a CPU-only Cloud Run gen2 service, and every build runs in its own throwaway sandbox process under a service account that holds no IAM roles. The film opens a built part, reads its true size and topology from the kernel, and shows the drawing sheet, sliders and files.
